text.p: Deere & Co. Tuesday reported record fourth-quarter and annual earnings as demand grew for its agricultural, industrial, commercial and consumer equipment worldwide.

Net income jumped 15 percent to $173.9 million, or 68 cents a share, for the quarter ended Oct. 31, from $150.6 million, or 57 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues grew 7 percent to $2.9 billion from $2.7 billion.
Profits for the fiscal year rose 16 percent to $817.3 million, or $3.14 a share, from $706.1 million, or $2.71 a share, last year. Revenues climbed 9 percent to $11.2 billion from $10.3 billion.
The results include a $15 million after-tax write-off in the fourth quarter to integrate and consolidate various Mexican operations.

"The company's operating margins remain strong as our focus on continuous improvement and growth is having a positive impact throughout our businesses," said Hans Becherer, chairman and chief executive officer of Deere.
Deere's stock slid, however, falling $2.75 to $43.875 on the New York Stock exchange in afternoon trading.

Moline, Ill.-based Deere said net sales to dealers of agricultural, industrial, commercial and consumer equipment rose to $2.49 billion in the fourth quarter from $2.34 billion in the year-ago period.

Export sales from the United States continued to grow, by 20 percent to $1.58 billion for 1996 from $1.31 billion last year. Overseas sales for the year remained very strong, rising by 26 percent to more than $2.5 billion for the first time in the company's history, Deere said.
Worldwide agricultural equipment operating profits jumped to $202 million for the quarter from $135 million in the year-ago period, and to $821 million for the year from $643 million in fiscal 1995.

Industrial equipment operating profit fell to $34 million for the fourth quarter from $36 million last year, and to $186 million for the year from $198 million. Deere cited increased development expenses associated with improving the fuel efficiency and emissions performance of new engines.

Worldwide commercial and consumer equipment operating profits fell to $1 million for the quarter from $35 million last year, and to $118 million for 1996 from $165 million a year ago. Deere blamed the drop on lower sales volume and increased promotional and growth expenditures.

Net income of Deere's financial services subsidiaries was $47.6 million for the quarter and $196.8 million for the entire year, Deere said. This was an improvement from $41 million in the 1995 fourth quarter and $166.6 million for the year.
